title: Negotiation heuristic index — personal draft
content:
Quick purpose: a compact index of what I actually care about when redlining MSA/SOWs for hosted API + Dedicated deals — not exhaustive, meant for negotiation pocket use. Keep this short, repeatable, and adaptable by account size.

Top-level priorities (fast filter):
- Safety of customer data & export control (data residency, export / transfer restrictions) — HIGH
- Operational continuity on termination (export timelines, transitional access, bulk export APIs) — HIGH
- Indemnity & liability caps + carveouts for willful misconduct — HIGH
- Audit rights & subprocessor transparency (90–180 day notice; narrow scope) — MED
- Service levels, rollback triggers, credit vs termination remedies — MED
- IP ownership of prompts/outputs (narrow language, customer retains output IP by default) — MED
- Subprocessor onboarding / flow-downs (SaaS + Dedicated differences) — LOW

Heuristic triage (how I call things quickly):
- If clause affects permanence of customer data or ability to export -> immediate escalation.
- If monetary cap < 12 months of committed fees for large enterprise -> push, propose 12x commit floor.
- If indemnity includes "any claim" language -> carve to third-party IP claims only + remove indirect.

Escalation triggers (who to loop in):
- Security/data residency wedge -> Solutions Eng + Infra lead (Priya) + Security (Sam).
- Broad IP assignments / ownership ask -> Research + Product counsel.
- Unilateral termination for convenience by vendor with no data/transition -> escalate to Sales leader for commercial trade.

Negotiation micro-scripts (short, human):
- On audit rights: "We agree on a limited, business-relevant audit. Can we scope to one yearly, remote-first, with pre-agreed checklist and minimal IRR?"
- On indemnity: "We accept responsibility for our willful misconduct and gross negligence. For IP claims, limited to direct damages and tied to actual use of our service."
- On data export: "Customer must be able to export all customer data within 30 days in machine-readable formats; vendor will assist with a migration runbook where needed."

Quick redline snippets (compatible phrasing to drop in):
- Data export: "Upon termination or upon Customer's written request, Vendor will make available all Customer Data in commonly used machine-readable formats within thirty (30) days and shall not withhold export for any reason other than confirmed outstanding fees; reasonable assistance to transfer shall be provided under a separate SOW if needed."
- Indemnity carve: "Vendor's indemnity obligations exclude indirect, special, consequential or punitive damages. Vendor's liability for IP claims shall not exceed the greater of (i) direct damages proven, or (ii) $X, except where liability arises from willful misconduct or gross negligence."
- Audit: "Customer may conduct one (1) remote audit per rolling 12-month period with 30 days' prior notice. On-site audits require mutual agreement and cost allocation if scope exceeds normal compliance checks."

Tactical notes:
- Use canary concessions: give up audit frequency in exchange for stronger data export language.
- Metered remedies vs termination: prefer credits + cure periods except for material security incidents.
- Avoid absolute blanket rights (e.g., unlimited termination for convenience) without pro-rata refund.

Open questions to resolve with team before speaking to counterparty:
- What is our default $X cap threshold for early-stage vs enterprise? (set standard language)
- Do we accept a parent guarantee for SMBs? When to require?
- Exact subprocessor notice window (30 vs 60 days) and required flow-downs for Dedicated deployments.

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally terse. Convert repeated language into a small clause library (one-line keys) and store in Confluence once stabilized. For urgent redlines, copy top snippets and add account-specific notes.

Recent example references:
- SOW with BetaCustomer: pushed export timeline from 60 -> 30 days; swapped on-site audit for remote-first + sampling.
- Enterprise MSA with BigBank: negotiated carve on indemnity for third-party IP only; required solutions-eng time for transition SOW.

Last quick checklist before sending counter:
[ ] Data export clause present and 30d timeline
[ ] Indemnity limited to IP/third-party + carveouts for indirect
[ ] Liability cap defined and matches commercial tier
[ ] Audit scope narrow and remote-first
[ ] Termination remedies: cure + credits vs immediate termination for non-security issues

End of notes — keep this as a daily-use pocket index and evolve with patterns observed in 10–15 deals.
